scope: Static new-feature screenshot review, both Windows path layouts at hosted 96 DPI

captures.finding: Two workflow names, availability and action buttons readable; inputs/expected answers visible; long details/notice use visible native scrollbars.
Editable graph and tool options present; toolbar and footer readable; graph clipping/ellipses reflect the scrollable canvas viewport.
Search, selected analysis, status, sample, timestamp and measured counts readable. Long tool column is intentionally ellipsized; full summary is scrollable.
Failed execution state, real missing-file error and next action readable; missing results-folder action disabled.
Scrolled error/action and no-invented-QC-threshold interpretation visible without overlap.
Clear empty-state explanation; View and Open buttons visibly disabled; Search and Close readable.

spaces.reviewType: Independent visual inspection of six exact-candidate spaced-path Windows captures
spaces.summary: No visible control overlap or clipped fixed labels/action text. Observed partial long text, card labels and table cells are explained by scrollable viewports or explicit ellipses.

findings: Two workflow names, requirements states, section labels and all four action buttons are readable and separated.

Input descriptions and fixture expected answers are readable. Further details and the longer training notice continue within visible vertical-scroll panes; their lower-edge clipping is viewport behavior, not lost fixed labels.
Navigation, workflow controls, input/source connections, selected-tool fields, action buttons and loaded-workflow status are readable without overlap.

The 100% workflow canvas extends beyond its viewport with horizontal and vertical scrollbars; card headings use ellipses. These are intentional navigation/truncation treatments. The complete DAG is not visible in this single capture.
Search query, selected completed result, sample, start time, summary heading and result actions are readable.
Recorded metric counts are visible with the explicit no-QC-verdict label. Tools cell text is ellipsized to its column and remaining summary details continue in a vertical-scroll pane.
The named failed result and failed execution state are visible. The actual missing-file cause and corrective replacement-input guidance fit inside the summary pane.
The folder action is visibly disabled for preparation failure. Long tool-list text uses table ellipsis; additional explanation continues below the scrollable summary viewport.
The scrolled summary visibly shows the missing-input cause, complete corrective action, unavailable measurements and interpretation limits.
Wrapping stays within the text pane, and fixed search/status/action controls remain unobstructed.
The unmatched query, empty table, explicit no-matching-result message and zero-result notice are readable.
View saved workflow and Open results folder are visibly disabled; Search and Close remain available. No prior result details remain visible.

limits: Static hosted Windows Server 2022 captures at 96 DPI only; no high-DPI, smaller-screen, multi-monitor, physical trackpad or representative-machine acceptance claim.
Visual review does not independently execute interactions, inspect intermediate repaint frames or prove keyboard/scroll behavior; the separately recorded native gate covers its stated interactions.
Only the visible portions of long details and the workflow canvas were inspected; this review does not claim the complete DAG or every scrolled line was visible.
Scientific correctness and full suite results remain the separately recorded gate evidence; visual legibility is not biological or clinical validation.
Long details and DAG intentionally use scrollable viewports; no full graph visibility at one zoom implied.
No high-DPI, physical trackpad, multi-monitor, temporal-rendering or representative-PC acceptance inferred.
